newsitem.title: USA: AM Intl in merger pact with Pacholder.
newsitem.headline: AM Intl in merger pact with Pacholder.

text.p: AM International Inc said on Tuesday it has entered into a merger agreement with Pacholder Associates Inc, under which AM shareholders will receive $5 per common share.
Under the agreement, AM International will merge with a unit of Pacholder and become a wholly owned subsidiary.

The transaction is subject to Pacholder finalizing a credit facility within 30 days and other conditions, AM said, including the approval by a majority of AM shareholders at a meeting tentatively scheduled for January 1997.

AM currently has about 800 employees. The company's business now consists of the domestic operations of its AM Multigraphics segment, a distributor of equipment, supplies and services to the graphic arts industry.

AM recently completed the sale of substantially all of the assets of its Sheridan Systems division, and the sale of its interest in AM Japan Co Ltd. In 1996, the company divested its unprofitable European subsidiaries, and its unprofitable Canadian subsidiary initiated bankruptcy proceedings earlier this month, the company said.
On October 28, AM shares closed at 2-3/4.
"This is a very favorable transaction for our shareholders, employees, and for the business as a whole," said AM International chairman, president and chief executive Jerome Brady.

"The purchase price of $5 per share represents a significant premium over current market value, and the new owners of the business will be positioned to focus on the domestic distribution and service capabilities and potential of the AM Multigraphics business," Brady said.
AM said the current president of AM Multigraphics and vice president and chief financial officer of AM International, Thomas Rooney, will serve as president of the merged companies.
Rooney has worked with AM for more than 22 years.
AM International will transfer its remaining corporate activity, currently in Rosemont, Ill., to its Multigraphics headquarters in Mount Prospect, Ill., the company said.
